title: Vishnu and Shiva (Hindu mythology)
subtitle: Hindu mythology
subject: mythologie
description: Create, preserve, destroy to be reborn: Vishnu and Shiva, pillars of Trimurti, turn the cyclical time of Hinduism.

hero.hook: One descends to Earth to save the order. The other dances to burn everything and start again. Together, they make the universe last.

blocks.text: In Hindu mythology, time is not a straight line. It is a series of cycles. At the top is the : three functions for the same principle. **Brahma** creates. **Vishnu** preserves. **Shiva** destroyed to allow renewal. [[Trimurti]]

This course follows Vishnu and Shiva, the two most living pillars of this trinity. Their attributes, their incarnations and their symbolism show how Hinduism reconciles life and death, order and transformation.

sections.title: The Trimurti, three faces of the same principle

blocks.text: The multiple gods are faces of an ultimate reality called . The Trimurti gives three useful forms. **Brahma** generates the universe at the beginning of each cycle; his role then ends, which explains why he is little venerated today in India. [[Brahman]]

blocks.caption: Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva: create, preserve, transform.

blocks.text: **Vishnu** ensures that the order holds. **Shiva** destroys what is worn out or corrupted. This destruction is not an absolute evil: it makes way for a new cycle. A “day of Brahma” lasts billions of years. Nothing is really lost; everything starts again.
A single “day of Brahma” (a Kalpa) lasts **4.32 trillion** years, a duration eerily close to the age of the Earth estimated by modern science.

**Vishnu** protects the , the moral and cosmic law. When evil threatens to take over, he descends to Earth in the form of **avatar**. The  tradition has ten, first animal, then human. [[Dharma]] [[Dashavatar]]

blocks.caption: Krishna, avatar of Vishnu: wisdom, love and just war.

blocks.text: Among them, king **Rama** embodies virtue; **Krishna**, divine wisdom and love. Hinduism has even integrated the **Buddha** as the ninth avatar. The tenth, **Kalki**, will come on a white horse to close the dark age of . [[Kali Yuga]]
Since the 1980s, digital pioneers have borrowed the word “avatar” to designate the representation of a user in a virtual world.

**Shiva** is the god of paradoxes: ascetic covered in ashes on Mount , and yet husband of **Parvati**, father of **Ganesha**. He embodies the energy that transforms, especially through dance. [[Kailash]]

blocks.caption: Nataraja: Shiva dances between creation and destruction.

blocks.text: In the form of **Nataraja**, “king of dance”, he performs the **Tandava**. In one hand, the  marks the rhythm of creation; in the other, the fire of destruction. One foot crushes ignorance; the other, raised, offers liberation. Change is the only constant. [[Damaru]]
At CERN in Geneva, a statue of Nataraja offered by India reminds particle physicists of this dance: perpetual creation and destruction of the universe.

Vishnu structures and guides through his incarnations. Shiva liberates by breaking illusions and attachments. Together, they make  not a prison, but a path: to be reborn, to act, to progress. [[Samsara and karma]]

From this duality are born **vishnuism** and **shiivism**, currents which enrich each other rather than clash, particularly around . In this vision, each end prepares a departure. [[The Bhagavad Gita]]

The **Trimurti** harmonizes the universe: Brahma creates, Vishnu preserves through his avatars, Shiva destroys to be reborn. Cyclical vision where karma and samsara make each destruction the prelude to a new cycle.
